title: Women's T20 Asia Cup 2026: India Eye Title Reclaim as Tournament Opens in Dubai
excerpt: Harmanpreet Kaur leads a 15-member squad into the continental T20 tournament starting August 28, with the marquee India-Pakistan clash set for September 5.
body:
• The Women's T20 Asia Cup 2026 runs from August 28 to September 13 in Dubai, featuring eight teams across two groups with all matches at the Dubai International Stadium.
  • India, seven-time champions, open against Thailand on August 30 and face Pakistan in the marquee group-stage clash on September 5.
  • Jemimah Rodrigues has been ruled out with a high-grade hamstring tear, with Pratika Rawal named as her replacement in the 15-member squad.
  • Defending champions Sri Lanka, who beat India in the 2024 final, are in Group B alongside Bangladesh, UAE, and debutants Indonesia.

Tournament Format and Schedule

The 10th edition of the Women's Asia Cup, and the sixth to be held in the T20 format, begins on August 28 when Thailand face Hong Kong China at the Dubai International Stadium. All 15 matches—including the semi-finals and final—will be played at the same venue under lights.

Eight teams have been split into two groups. Group A features India, Pakistan, Thailand, and Hong Kong China. Group B comprises Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, hosts UAE, and Indonesia, who make their Women's Asia Cup debut after qualifying through the ACC pathway.

The top two teams from each group advance to the semi-finals on September 10 and 11, with the final scheduled for September 13. All matches are set to begin at 8:00 PM IST.

India's Squad and Key Absences

The Board of Control for Cricket in India named Harmanpreet Kaur as captain of a 15-member squad, with Smriti Mandhana serving as vice-captain. The experienced core includes explosive opener Shafali Verma, all-rounder Deepti Sharma, and wicketkeeper-batter Richa Ghosh.

The biggest absence is Jemimah Rodrigues, a key middle-order batter who has been ruled out after suffering a high-grade hamstring tear. Pratika Rawal, originally named in the reserve list, has been called up as her replacement.

The pace attack will be spearheaded by Renuka Singh Thakur alongside Arundhati Reddy, while Radha Yadav, Sree Charani, Kranti Gaud, and Nandni Sharma provide spin options. G. Kamalini serves as the second wicketkeeping option behind Ghosh.

India's Path Through the Group Stage

India begin their campaign against Thailand on August 30, followed by a fixture against Hong Kong China on September 3. The blockbuster encounter against Pakistan comes on September 5 in what will be the most-watched match of the group stage.

India are the most successful team in Women's Asia Cup history, winning seven of the nine editions played so far. Their dominance, however, was broken in the 2024 edition when Sri Lanka defeated them in the final.

"The top two teams from each group will qualify for the semi-finals, with the final set for September 13. All matches will be held at the Dubai International Stadium under lights."

— Asian Cricket Council

Key Rivals and Players to Watch

Pakistan, led by Fatima Sana, will be eager to improve on their record against India in Asia Cup finals—they finished runners-up in 2012 and 2016, losing to India on both occasions. Sadia Iqbal's bowling performance at the 2026 Women's T20 World Cup signals Pakistan's growing competitiveness.

Sri Lanka enter as defending champions and title favorites in Group B, led by the experienced Chamari Athapaththu. Bangladesh, winners of the 2018 edition, round out the realistic contenders.

Indonesia's inclusion as debutants marks a significant step for ACC's efforts to expand the women's game across Asia. The tournament also serves as crucial preparation ahead of the upcoming Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya.

What's at Stake for India

For India, this tournament arrives after a disappointing group-stage exit at the 2026 Women's T20 World Cup, where defeats to South Africa and Australia ended their campaign early. The Asia Cup presents an opportunity to rebuild confidence and reassert their continental dominance before the Asian Games, where they are defending champions.

With the tournament just two days away, all eyes will be on whether Harmanpreet Kaur's squad can handle the pressure of expectation and reclaim a title they have made their own over the past two decades.
